sections.title: Introduction to the WHO PrEP implementation tool

summary.text: Introduces the WHO PrEP implementation tool, developed after WHO's 2015 recommendation to offer oral PrEP to people at substantial HIV risk. It stresses that individual risk varies, that people requesting PrEP should be prioritized, that barriers faced by key populations should be addressed and that the choice to use PrEP rests with the individual.

sections.extract: 1 HIV acquisition risk varies considerably within populations and geographical locations. Population-level HIV incidence is an important determinant of individual-level risk of HIV acquisition. However, when considering who could benefit from PrEP, it is important to take into account the characteristics and behaviours of individuals and their partners that could lead to HIV exposure. Even in locations with a low

sections.title: Audience and scope of the tool

summary.text: Explains that the PrEP tool is a set of modules for different stakeholders and that this STI integration module compiles existing WHO guidance without making new recommendations.

sections.extract: The HIV PrEP implementation tool contains modules for a range of stakeholders to support them in the consideration, planning, introduction, implementation and roll-out of PrEP. The modules can be used on their own or in combination. In addition, there is a module for individuals interested in or already taking oral PrEP. This module does not make any new recommendations. It compiles existing WHO recommendations,

sections.title: Guiding principles

summary.text: Sets out guiding principles for offering PrEP through a public health, human rights and people-centred approach and quotes WHO's definition of sexual health.

sections.extract: It is important to adopt an evidence-based public health, human rights, and people- and community-centred approach when offering PrEP. Such an approach is aligned with principles of universal health coverage, gender equality and health-related rights, including accessibility, availability, acceptability and quality of services for people who need PrEP. Placing the people and communities who could benefit from PrEP

sections.title: The module on PrEP and STI service integration

summary.text: Introduces the module on integrating STI services with PrEP and lists in a box serious consequences of sexually transmitted infections such as congenital syphilis, HPV-related cancers, infertility and chronic hepatitis.

sections.extract: Many bacteria, viruses and parasites are known to be transmitted through sexual contact. Some have a major impact on sexual, reproductive and neonatal health and can result in severe or life- threatening complications if not detected and treated in a timely manner (see Box 1). Box 1. sections.title: Epidemiology of STIs

summary.text: Gives global figures for curable STIs, estimating 374 million new cases in 2020, along with congenital syphilis, genital herpes and HPV-related cervical cancer, most occurring in low- and middle-income countries. It also explains that the module has two parts, for programme managers and for facility managers and health workers.

sections.extract: In 2020 there were approximately 374 million estimated incident cases of four curable STIs – syphilis, caused by Treponema pallidum (6 million cases); gonorrhoea, caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae (87 million cases); Chlamydia trachomatis (127 million cases); and Trichomonas vaginalis (156 million cases) (6). (6,7). Syphilis during pregnancy caused an estimated annual 661 000 cases of congenital syphilis, including

sections.title: High burden of STIs and associated factors among people on HIV PrEP

summary.text: Reviews evidence that STI prevalence and incidence are high among people on PrEP, including men who have sex with men and young African women, compared with general population estimates. It discusses contributing factors such as sexual networks, condom use, stigma and background prevalence.

sections.extract: A systematic review of the STI burden among people accessing PrEP, predominantly men who have sex with men, showed that STI prevalence prior to starting PrEP was high (12% for gonorrhoea, 11% for chlamydia, 5% for active syphilis and 24% for any of the three). STI incidence remained high at follow-up visits for PrEP refills (11). For comparison, the estimated global prevalence in 2020 of these STIs among persons

sections.title: Why integrate STI services?

summary.text: Explains the reasons for integrating STI services into PrEP, including reaching people with asymptomatic infections, efficiency gains, people-centred care and tackling antimicrobial resistance in gonorrhoea. It links integration to global targets for reducing STIs, congenital syphilis and cervical cancer deaths by 2030.

sections.extract: Offering STI services to PrEP clients creates an important opportunity for people to benefit from such services who otherwise may not access STI testing and treatment, particularly those at high risk of infection and are asymptomatic (28,29). Integrating STIs services into PrEP services, as well as offering PrEP to people seeking STI and related services, fosters synergies and efficiencies in the public health

summary.text: A section heading for Part 1 of the module, on integration of STI services for programme managers and other decision-makers.

sections.title: Planning for integration

summary.text: Describes using the differentiated service delivery framework to plan which STI services to integrate with PrEP, and how, by whom and where they are offered.

sections.extract: Differentiated service delivery (DSD) is a person-centred approach that simplifies and adapts PrEP and STI services to meet clients’ needs and situations (2). DSD can ensure that the health system functions efficiently, enable the health system to focus resources on those most in need and, most importantly, enhance client outcomes. Considering the WHO DSD framework (35) and its adaptation for the provision of PrEP

sections.title: How to integrate STI services?

summary.text: Recommends a stepwise approach to integrating STI services with PrEP, adapted to local context and moving from symptom-based to cause-based management.

sections.extract: A stepwise approach to the integration of STI services with PrEP services should be considered (Fig. 2). This approach should be informed by the local context, including epidemiology, availability of resources and acceptability to users and health care workers. When the information is available, the cost-effectiveness of the different levels of STI services provided should be considered. Through this stepwise

sections.title: What STI services to integrate?

summary.text: Explains that STI services should be added gradually and adapted to each PrEP delivery model, from digital to facility-based, with examples in an annex.

sections.extract: Although it is not currently feasible to offer STI services to all people on PrEP everywhere, the gradual addition of services using a stepwise approach can encourage and advance integration of STI services. Particular STI services will need to be adapted to PrEP service delivery models (from digital health/virtual interventions (36,37) to facility-based models with laboratory infrastructure) as well as to the local

sections.title: Where to integrate STI services?

summary.text: Notes that STI services chosen for integration must suit the PrEP delivery model and local resources, laws and regulations.

sections.extract: Currently, programmes offer PrEP through a variety of service delivery models. The STI services selected for integration should be feasible for the specific model of PrEP delivery as well as aligned with local resources, laws and regulations. Annex 2 also provides examples of different combinations of STI services and where and how they can be offered to people who use PrEP.

sections.title: Who should offer integrated services?

summary.text: Discusses which health workers can deliver integrated PrEP and STI services, stressing task sharing with peers and lay providers, and shows a stepwise diagram from syndromic management to testing and vaccination. A case study describes integrated PrEP and STI services for key populations at a government health centre in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

sections.extract: As a range of health care workers may deliver PrEP, including trained peers and other lay providers, task shifting and task sharing are important to PrEP and STI service integration and scale-up (38). Along with increasing access, they may generate health system efficiencies and support models of service provision that are more acceptable to people on PrEP. Fig. 2. Simplified programmatic stepwise approach to

sections.title: Human resources and capacity building

summary.text: Describes the staffing and training needed to add STI services to PrEP delivery, such as training on diagnostic algorithms, case management and antimicrobial resistance. It also outlines the role of peers and community workers in linking clients to care and supporting adherence.

sections.extract: The human resources required to offer STI services to people who access PrEP will vary according to the characteristics of existing PrEP delivery models, including but not limited to the different cadres of health care workers, the possibility of task sharing and task shifting (38), engagement of peer and community health care workers, as well as local laws and regulations on the qualifications required to provide

sections.title: Costs

summary.text: Argues that integrating PrEP and STI services can improve efficiency and draw HIV funding into the underfunded STI response, while noting extra costs for staff, training and supplies. It highlights the cost-effectiveness of dual HIV/syphilis tests and presents a Pan American Health Organization costing tool with an example comparing budget scenarios for 2021–2025.

sections.extract: Integrating the delivery of PrEP and STI services can increase efficiency in the use of national resources. Furthermore, considering that, historically, HIV programmes are fairly well-funded, offering integrated STI services to people on PrEP creates an opportunity to leverage additional funding and resources for the STI response, which typically is underfunded. It is critical for PrEP programmes to consider a range

sections.title: Documentation, monitoring and evaluation

summary.text: Stresses documenting and monitoring STI services for PrEP users within existing reporting systems while protecting confidentiality, and points to suggested indicators. A case study from Namibia describes an online platform used to promote testing and manage HIV and STI services for key populations.

sections.extract: Documentation, monitoring and evaluation of the provision of STI services for people on PrEP are essential to assess service performance and adjust interventions in a timely manner. For countries that do not have a system that can capture STI data, monitoring questions related to STIs can be incorporated into existing PrEP-related reporting systems (for example, sexual history taking) and do not need to be developed

sections.title: Demand generation for STI services among people accessing PrEP

summary.text: Explains the need to generate demand for STI services among PrEP users, since most STIs are asymptomatic, and to involve communities in designing messages. A case study describes a Brazilian project that used social media and a chatbot to reach adolescents from key populations.

sections.extract: Like demand generation for HIV PrEP (see WHO PrEP implementation tool Module 2: community educators and advocates (48)), creating demand for STI services is critical. It can raise awareness of STI signs and symptoms and potential exposure to an STI, as well as promote care-seeking behaviours such as regular STI testing and notifying partners of an STI diagnosis. This is particularly relevant as most STIs do not

sections.title: Preparing for upcoming innovations

summary.text: Describes upcoming innovations that may ease integrated PrEP and STI services, including syphilis and dual HIV/syphilis self-tests, rapid tests for active syphilis and multiplex point-of-care platforms. It also mentions prevention innovations and vaccines and tests in development, noting WHO has not yet issued recommendations on them.

sections.extract: Upcoming innovations may make the provision of integrated PrEP and STI services more efficient and acceptable and support scale-up. Currently, WHO does not have recommendations on these innovations. As evidence becomes available, WHO guidelines will be released. • Innovations in STI testing o Syphilis self-test and HIV/syphilis self-test. Self-tests have proved highly acceptable to both health care workers and

sections.title: Part 2. STI service delivery for facility managers and health care workers

summary.text: Opens Part 2 for facility managers and health workers, presenting an optimal package of STI services that can be integrated with PrEP and stressing that lack of STI services must never delay PrEP. It highlights the specific needs of adolescents and trans and gender diverse people and includes a schematic of STI case management.

sections.extract: care workers As mentioned in Part 1, different STI services can be integrated with PrEP services depending on how and where PrEP is offered and on local resources. Fig. 4 summarizes an optimal package of STI services that could be integrated at the facility level with laboratory support. In all contexts, however, inability to offer STI services should never delay or be a barrier to the provision of PrEP nor to

sections.title: Providing information and promoting health-seeking behaviours

summary.text: Advises giving PrEP clients basic STI information, including self-assessment of symptoms, and reminding them that PrEP does not protect against other STIs. It notes that some symptoms have non-STI causes, such as candidiasis and bacterial vaginosis.

sections.extract: During the first encounter with health services, clients should be provided with basic information on STIs (see Annex 4), including self-assessment for signs and symptoms (see example in Box 5) and prevention strategies (see section on STI Prevention). Additionally, due to the intense stigma associated with STIs, clients should know that some symptoms associated with STIs can be caused by other, non-STI-related

sections.title: Counselling

summary.text: Defines counselling as a non-judgemental exchange that helps clients make informed decisions, noting that WHO does not recommend counselling aimed at changing behaviour. A box describes higher-risk practices such as chemsex and use of dating apps.

sections.extract: Quality counselling is an essential component of client-centred care. Counselling is defined here as a non-judgemental interactive process between a trained health care worker or lay provider and a client during which information is exchanged and support is provided so that clients can make informed decisions, design a plan and take action to improve their health (58).1 For example, some behaviours associated with

sections.title: Prompting for signs and symptoms of STIs

summary.text: Stresses prompting clients to recognize STI signs and symptoms through self-assessment. A case study from South Africa describes adding symptom screening and a sub-study of laboratory STI testing to PrEP services for young people.

sections.extract: Prompting clients to notice STI signs and symptoms they may have is essential to promote health-seeking behaviours and to provide appropriate STI services, and it can be conducted as a self-assessment (see example in Box 5). 1 The definition for counselling used in this module is adapted from WHO’s Counselling for maternal and newborn health care: a handbook for building skills (58). WHO does not recommend

sections.title: STI prevention

summary.text: Summarizes WHO recommendations for STI prevention, mainly vaccines against hepatitis A, hepatitis B and HPV, and condoms with compatible lubricants. It notes the role of male circumcision and that post-exposure prophylaxis for bacterial STIs is recommended only after sexual assault.

sections.extract: Vaccines and condoms are the primary STI prevention tools (Table 1). In settings where voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) is recommended for HIV prevention, it also provides protection against some other STIs (63,64,65). Currently, WHO recommends post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for bacterial STIs only in the case of sexual assault/rape (66,67). Table 1. WHO recommendations for STI prevention Vaccines •

sections.title: STI testing

summary.text: Explains the options for STI testing, from laboratory and culture methods to rapid point-of-care and self-tests, and points to WHO laboratory guidance and prequalified diagnostics.

sections.extract: Some STIs can be diagnosed using etiologic laboratory methods, such as molecular tests. Etiologic diagnosis of syphilis is feasible in almost all settings. However, for other pathogens, etiologic diagnosis remains limited due to high costs. Alternatively, some STIs require the collection of samples and the culture of the pathogen under specific laboratory conditions, which also are not widely available. On the other

sections.title: Frequency of testing

summary.text: Discusses how often PrEP users should be tested for STIs, noting that self-testing and self-sampling can replace some visits and that evidence is insufficient for a general testing frequency. It suggests prioritizing regular testing for people at higher risk.

sections.extract: Optimal frequencies of STI testing vary by pathogen, population and epidemiologic context. Considering the WHO guidance for differentiated and simplified PrEP services, PrEP follow-up visits may vary between people on PrEP (2). For STIs, self- testing and self-sampling can be used between or in place of some clinic visits. For example, services that require PrEP clients to return every three months for a PrEP refill

sections.title: Considerations for syphilis testing and diagnosis

summary.text: Explains the complexity of diagnosing syphilis and the differences between treponemal and non-treponemal serological tests and their limitations. It mentions dual rapid tests that may help identify active infection.

sections.extract: Many people with syphilis do not have any symptoms or signs of infection, or health care providers may not notice signs and symptoms. Syphilis diagnosis is complex, usually requiring clients’ clinical and sexual history, physical examination and laboratory testing. The most widely available tests for syphilis are based on serology. These can be of two types: treponemal and non- treponemal tests. • Treponemal tests,

sections.title: Considerations for the diagnosis of gonorrhoea and chlamydia

summary.text: Discusses barriers to diagnosing gonorrhoea and chlamydia, such as the cost of molecular tests, and options like shared TB testing platforms and self-collected samples. It stresses sampling from the throat, rectum and genitals, citing studies showing many infections are missed otherwise, and includes a country example of pooled testing for key populations.

sections.extract: The costs of high-performance molecular POC tests for N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis remain prohibitive for many low- and middle-income countries posing an important barrier to increase testing coverage. Still, POC platforms for molecular testing are increasingly available in these countries for the diagnosis of tuberculosis (TB) and could be used for some STIs to optimize use of resources and increase testing

sections.title: Partner services

summary.text: Recommends offering partner services to people who test positive for HIV or STIs and describes strategies such as user referral, provider referral and contract referral, noting their effectiveness when combined with dual HIV/syphilis testing.

sections.extract: WHO recommends that providers offer assistance to clients who test positive for HIV to notify their partners and link them to care (40). Partner services’ strategies (such as assisted partner notification services) (see Box 8) are proven to be highly efficient and effective in detecting new cases and have already been adopted by several low- and middle-income countries. These strategies can also be used for STIs

sections.title: Consultation and physical examination

summary.text: Stresses the need for a private, supportive setting where clients can talk openly about their sexual history, which helps judge STI risk in PrEP services, while noting that history-taking should not be a condition for getting PrEP or STI care.

sections.extract: To establish a correct diagnosis, the health care provider needs to ensure that there is a conducive environment to enable people to discuss their sexual history freely. Taking a sexual and medical history is also central to providing quality PrEP and STI care, and it is an important component of people-centred care. Obtaining clients’ sexual history will help providers to gauge a person’s likelihood of being

sections.title: Physical examination

summary.text: Sets out how to prepare for and conduct a respectful physical examination for STIs, with consent, privacy, a chaperone and the option of self-collected samples, and lists what to look for in the mouth, skin, genitals and anal area. A case study from Nigeria describes donor-supported cryotherapy for anogenital warts in one-stop clinics for key populations and the cost and liquid nitrogen problems that threaten its sustainability.

sections.extract: Prior to the physical examination, the user should: • be informed about the examination procedure (exposure of abdomen, genitals and thighs); • give consent for the examination. During the examination, the user should be: • examined in a private space with the presence of a chaperone; if a chaperone is not available, the health care provider should ask the user’s consent to be examined without a chaperone; • covered

sections.title: Syndromic approach

summary.text: Explains the syndromic approach to STIs, which treats groups of symptoms for their most likely causes but can lead to both over- and undertreatment. It notes WHO's 2021 guideline recommends treatment based on molecular tests where possible and syndromic management where testing is limited, with flow charts for five syndromes.

sections.extract: The syndromic approach identifies consistent groups of symptoms and easily recognized signs (syndromes –for example, vaginal discharge, urethral discharge, genital ulcers, abdominal pain) and treats for the most likely organisms producing the syndrome. Syndromic case management can result in both overtreatment, because there are other causes of syndromes not related to an STI, and undertreatment, as the majority of

sections.title: Specific treatment for common STIs

summary.text: Calls for correct STI treatment ideally on the first visit, rapid treatment of partners and counselling on medicines and adherence, using standard protocols to limit antimicrobial resistance. It points to WHO treatment guidelines for chlamydia, herpes, gonorrhoea, syphilis, syphilis in pregnancy and HPV-related cervical lesions.

sections.extract: Correct and effective STI treatment should be provided and taken, ideally, on the day of first contact between clients and health care providers. Rapid treatment of sexual partners is also critical to avoid reinfection and to break the chain of transmission, which could include expedited partner treatment. A client who is prescribed treatment for an STI should be counselled on medication information, risks and

sections.title: Clinical follow-up

summary.text: Explains that clinical follow-up is mainly for people whose symptoms persist after treatment and lists reasons for treatment failure, such as poor adherence, reinfection, antimicrobial resistance and other untreated infections. Footnotes note that WHO is revising gonorrhoea treatment because of growing resistance.

sections.extract: Follow-up is generally limited to those with persistent symptoms after a stipulated period after the recommended treatment. Clients may return for further assessment if the condition has not resolved or it has recurred. The health care provider will need to determine the reason for the user’s return to guide next steps (see Box 10). Box 10. Reasons for STI treatment failure that need to be assessed to guide further

sections.title: Referrals and linkage to care

summary.text: Discusses referral of people with STIs to other levels of care and the risk of losing them to follow-up, which makes same-day treatment especially valuable. It lists strategies to support linkage, such as non-judgemental and flexible services, self-collection, free care, peer support, digital tools and clear national policies. A case study from South Africa describes client preferences, showing most favour self-led STI services but some prefer provider-led care, so services should offer choice.

sections.extract: Sometimes people diagnosed with an STI will need to be referred to another level of care. For example, someone with an abnormality in the anorectal area may need to be referred to a colorectal surgeon or oncologist or for diagnostic tests. Health care workers should be provided with clear and easily accessible information on referral and counter-referral mechanisms.1 However, when referring someone to another

sections.title: Outbreaks of STIs and other infections that can be sexually transmissible

summary.text: Describes rising outbreaks of syphilis, gonorrhoea including extensively drug-resistant strains, lymphogranuloma venereum, HIV and other sexually transmissible infections such as Shigella, E. coli, hepatitis A, B and C and monkeypox, reported mainly among men who have sex with men in high-income countries. A box sets out how monkeypox spreads, its symptoms and differential diagnosis, contact tracing and vaccination of contacts soon after exposure. It ends by warning against stigmatizing affected groups and noting that PrEP services can help detect and report surges in infections.

sections.extract: There has been an increase in outbreaks of syphilis, gonorrhoea (including extensive drug resistance (XDR)1 by gonococci), LVG and HIV, as well as other pathogens not classified as STIs but that are transmissible through sexual contact, reported mostly by high-income countries among men who have sex with men. sections.title: Annex 1. WHO guidance and guidelines relevant to integrating STI services into PrEP

summary.text: Lists the WHO guidelines and guidance this STI integration module aligns with, grouped by key populations, STIs, cervical cancer, viral hepatitis and strategic information, with their full references. These include guidelines on symptomatic STI management, self-collection of samples, syphilis in pregnancy, treatment of specific STIs, cervical pre-cancer screening and hepatitis B and C testing and care.

sections.title: Annex 2. Examples of possible PrEP service delivery models and potential integration of STI services.

summary.text: Presents a table showing which STI services, such as counselling, partner services, rapid tests, self-sampling, molecular testing, vaccination, treatment and referral, could be offered through different PrEP delivery models, from virtual platforms and home delivery to pharmacies, mobile units and facilities with or without laboratories. Notes explain the abbreviations and that implementation depends on local context and national rules.

sections.extract: STI services. PrEP service delivery models can be combined to increase the range of STI services provided, such as digital health platforms with home delivery. All the examples provided of PrEP service delivery models and STI service integration to be implemented will depend on local context and on national norms and regulations. PrEP delivery platforms STI services Virtual intervention platforms (1) Home delivery

sections.title: Annex 3. STI priority indicators

summary.text: Sets out core STI indicators for PrEP and HIV services, giving short names, definitions, numerators and denominators for testing coverage, test positivity and treatment coverage for syphilis, gonorrhoea and other infections. It also includes an indicator on STI incidence among people using PrEP measured per person-years and cites WHO strategic information guidelines. Each indicator is designed to be tracked over a reporting period.

summary.text: Tabulates the main pathogens relevant to people using PrEP, such as chlamydia, herpes, genital mycoplasmas, hepatitis A, B and C, HPV, lymphogranuloma venereum, gonorrhoea, syphilis and trichomonas, showing whether each is curable and how it is transmitted. Footnotes clarify points such as suppressive therapy for herpes and hepatitis B.

sections.title: Annex 5. Summary of WHO guidance for testing and treatment for selected pathogens that can be transmitted through sex

summary.text: Summarises WHO-recommended diagnostic tests and first-line treatments for selected sexually transmissible pathogens, including chlamydia, herpes, Mycoplasma genitalium, hepatitis B and C, gonorrhoea and syphilis. It gives drug regimens and notes such as pooling samples from three sites, preferring doxycycline for anorectal chlamydia and avoiding it in pregnancy. The table's WHO guideline references and contact details for WHO's global HIV, hepatitis and STI programmes close the document.

narratives.en: Cover photograph of a colourful painted mural on a clinic wall headed 'NGANGELIZWE CHC'. A heart reads 'We are the generation that will end HIV', with slogans 'She conquers' and 'Love yourself!', the handles '@myPrEP_SA' and '@myPrEPSouthAfrica', and a painted young woman in a 'b-wise' T-shirt making a peace sign.
narratives.ar: صورة الغلاف لجدارية ملونة مرسومة على جدار عيادة يتصدرها اسم 'NGANGELIZWE CHC'. يحمل قلب عبارة 'نحن الجيل الذي سينهي فيروس العوز المناعي البشري'، مع شعارات 'She conquers' و'Love yourself!'، والحسابين '@myPrEP_SA' و'@myPrEPSouthAfrica'، ورسم لشابة ترتدي قميصاً مكتوباً عليه 'b-wise' وتشير بعلامة السلام.
narratives.zh: 封面照片：诊所墙上一幅色彩鲜艳的壁画，顶部写有“NGANGELIZWE CHC”。一颗心形图案上写着“我们是将终结艾滋病毒的一代”，另有标语“She conquers”和“Love yourself!”、账号“@myPrEP_SA”和“@myPrEPSouthAfrica”，以及一位身穿“b-wise”T恤、比出和平手势的年轻女性画像。
narratives.es: Fotografía de portada de un colorido mural pintado en la pared de un centro de salud con el encabezado «NGANGELIZWE CHC». Un corazón dice «Somos la generación que pondrá fin al VIH», con los lemas «She conquers» y «Love yourself!», las cuentas «@myPrEP_SA» y «@myPrEPSouthAfrica», y una joven pintada con una camiseta «b-wise» haciendo el signo de la paz.
narratives.fr: Photo de couverture d'une fresque colorée peinte sur le mur d'un centre de santé, intitulée « NGANGELIZWE CHC ». Un cœur porte l'inscription « Nous sommes la génération qui mettra fin au VIH », avec les slogans « She conquers » et « Love yourself! », les comptes « @myPrEP_SA » et « @myPrEPSouthAfrica », et une jeune femme peinte vêtue d'un tee-shirt « b-wise » faisant le signe de la paix.
narratives.ru: Фотография на обложке: красочная роспись на стене медицинского учреждения с надписью «NGANGELIZWE CHC». На сердце написано «Мы — поколение, которое покончит с ВИЧ», рядом лозунги «She conquers» и «Love yourself!», аккаунты «@myPrEP_SA» и «@myPrEPSouthAfrica» и нарисованная молодая женщина в футболке «b-wise», показывающая знак мира.

narratives.en: Cover photograph of two women seated indoors; one, in a pink shirt, holds up a strip of condom packets while speaking.
narratives.ar: صورة الغلاف لامرأتين جالستين في مكان مغلق؛ إحداهما ترتدي قميصاً وردياً وترفع شريطاً من عبوات الواقيات الذكرية وهي تتحدث.
narratives.zh: 封面照片：两名女性坐在室内，其中一位身穿粉色上衣，一边说话一边举起一排安全套包装。
narratives.es: Fotografía de portada de dos mujeres sentadas en un interior; una de ellas, con camisa rosa, sostiene una tira de preservativos mientras habla.
narratives.fr: Photo de couverture de deux femmes assises à l'intérieur ; l'une, en chemise rose, montre une bande de préservatifs tout en parlant.
narratives.ru: Фотография на обложке: две женщины сидят в помещении; одна из них, в розовой рубашке, держит в руках ленту упаковок презервативов и что-то рассказывает.

narratives.en: Cover photograph of four people sitting together outdoors in front of a brick building, talking and smiling.
narratives.ar: صورة الغلاف لأربعة أشخاص يجلسون معاً في الهواء الطلق أمام مبنى من الطوب، يتحدثون ويبتسمون.
narratives.zh: 封面照片：四个人在一栋砖楼前的户外坐在一起，交谈并微笑。
narratives.es: Fotografía de portada de cuatro personas sentadas juntas al aire libre frente a un edificio de ladrillo, conversando y sonriendo.
narratives.fr: Photo de couverture de quatre personnes assises ensemble en plein air devant un bâtiment en brique, en train de discuter et de sourire.
narratives.ru: Фотография на обложке: четыре человека сидят вместе на улице перед кирпичным зданием, разговаривают и улыбаются.

narratives.en: Cover photograph of a smiling health worker in a white uniform in a pharmacy store room, holding a box of tablets, with shelves of medicine boxes behind her.
narratives.ar: صورة الغلاف لعاملة صحية مبتسمة ترتدي زياً أبيض في مخزن صيدلية، تحمل علبة أقراص، وخلفها رفوف عليها علب أدوية.
narratives.zh: 封面照片：一名身穿白色制服、面带微笑的卫生工作者在药房库房中手持一盒片剂，身后是摆满药盒的货架。
narratives.es: Fotografía de portada de una trabajadora sanitaria sonriente con uniforme blanco en el almacén de una farmacia, que sostiene una caja de comprimidos, con estantes de cajas de medicamentos detrás.
narratives.fr: Photo de couverture d'une agente de santé souriante en uniforme blanc dans la réserve d'une pharmacie, tenant une boîte de comprimés, avec des étagères de boîtes de médicaments derrière elle.
narratives.ru: Фотография на обложке: улыбающаяся медицинская работница в белой форме на складе аптеки держит коробку таблеток; за ней полки с коробками лекарств.

narratives.en: Cover photograph taken from behind a motorbike rider on a city street; the delivery box on the back reads 'I ♥ PrEP' and carries the logos of USAID, PATH and partner organizations.
narratives.ar: صورة الغلاف ملتقطة من خلف سائق دراجة نارية في شارع بالمدينة؛ يحمل صندوق التوصيل الخلفي عبارة 'I ♥ PrEP' وشعارات الوكالة الأمريكية للتنمية الدولية (USAID) ومنظمة PATH ومنظمات شريكة.
narratives.zh: 封面照片：从城市街道上一名摩托车骑手身后拍摄；车后的送货箱上写着“I ♥ PrEP”，并印有美国国际开发署（USAID）、PATH及合作组织的标志。
narratives.es: Fotografía de portada tomada detrás de un motociclista en una calle urbana; la caja de reparto trasera dice «I ♥ PrEP» y lleva los logotipos de USAID, PATH y organizaciones asociadas.
narratives.fr: Photo de couverture prise derrière un motocycliste dans une rue ; le coffre de livraison arrière porte l'inscription « I ♥ PrEP » et les logos de l'USAID, de PATH et d'organisations partenaires.
narratives.ru: Фотография на обложке, снятая сзади мотоциклиста на городской улице; на заднем ящике для доставки надпись «I ♥ PrEP» и логотипы USAID, PATH и организаций-партнеров.

narratives.en: Photograph of a hand in a blue laboratory glove holding a Petri dish with bacterial colonies streaked on red agar.
narratives.ar: صورة ليد ترتدي قفازاً مخبرياً أزرق تحمل طبق بتري عليه مستعمرات بكتيرية مخططة على وسط آغار أحمر.
narratives.zh: 照片：一只戴蓝色实验手套的手拿着培养皿，红色琼脂上划线接种有细菌菌落。
narratives.es: Fotografía de una mano con guante de laboratorio azul que sostiene una placa de Petri con colonias bacterianas sembradas en agar rojo.
narratives.fr: Photo d'une main gantée de bleu tenant une boîte de Petri contenant des colonies bactériennes ensemencées sur gélose rouge.
narratives.ru: Фотография: рука в синей лабораторной перчатке держит чашку Петри с бактериальными колониями, посеянными штрихом на красном агаре.

narratives.en: Diagram of the differentiated service delivery framework: four coloured blocks labelled 'HOW', 'WHERE', 'WHO' and 'WHAT' surround a central circle containing a person icon.
narratives.ar: مخطط لإطار تقديم الخدمات المتمايزة: أربع كتل ملونة معنونة 'كيف' و'أين' و'من' و'ماذا' تحيط بدائرة مركزية تحتوي على رمز شخص.
narratives.zh: 差异化服务提供框架示意图：标有“如何（HOW）”“何处（WHERE）”“何人（WHO）”和“什么（WHAT）”的四个彩色方块围绕着一个内含人形图标的中心圆。
narratives.es: Diagrama del marco de prestación diferenciada de servicios: cuatro bloques de color rotulados «CÓMO», «DÓNDE», «QUIÉN» y «QUÉ» rodean un círculo central con el icono de una persona.
narratives.fr: Schéma du cadre de prestation différenciée de services : quatre blocs de couleur intitulés « COMMENT », « OÙ », « QUI » et « QUOI » entourent un cercle central contenant une icône de personne.
narratives.ru: Схема рамочной модели дифференцированного предоставления услуг: четыре цветных блока с подписями «КАК», «ГДЕ», «КТО» и «ЧТО» окружают центральный круг с изображением человека.

narratives.en: Stepwise diagram along a horizontal arrow showing increasing levels of STI services: 'No STI services'; 'Syndromic management only (no tests available)'; 'Syndromic management + Testing using RDTs and treatment'; and 'Syndromic management + RDTs and molecular testing, treatment + Vaccination'.
narratives.ar: مخطط تدريجي على امتداد سهم أفقي يعرض مستويات متزايدة من خدمات العدوى المنقولة جنسياً: 'لا توجد خدمات للعدوى المنقولة جنسياً'؛ 'التدبير العلاجي المتلازمي فقط (لا تتوفر اختبارات)'؛ 'التدبير العلاجي المتلازمي + الاختبار باستخدام الاختبارات التشخيصية السريعة والعلاج'؛ و'التدبير العلاجي المتلازمي + الاختبارات التشخيصية السريعة والاختبارات الجزيئية والعلاج + التطعيم'.
narratives.zh: 沿水平箭头展开的阶梯式示意图，显示性传播感染服务的逐级提升：“无性传播感染服务”；“仅症状管理（无检测）”；“症状管理 + 使用快速诊断检测进行检测和治疗”；以及“症状管理 + 快速诊断检测和分子检测、治疗 + 疫苗接种”。
narratives.es: Diagrama escalonado a lo largo de una flecha horizontal que muestra niveles crecientes de servicios de ITS: «Sin servicios de ITS»; «Solo manejo sindrómico (sin pruebas disponibles)»; «Manejo sindrómico + pruebas con PDR y tratamiento»; y «Manejo sindrómico + PDR y pruebas moleculares, tratamiento + vacunación».
narratives.fr: Schéma par étapes le long d'une flèche horizontale montrant des niveaux croissants de services IST : « Aucun service IST » ; « Prise en charge syndromique uniquement (aucun test disponible) » ; « Prise en charge syndromique + dépistage par TDR et traitement » ; et « Prise en charge syndromique + TDR et tests moléculaires, traitement + vaccination ».
narratives.ru: Ступенчатая схема вдоль горизонтальной стрелки, показывающая возрастающие уровни услуг в связи с ИППП: «Нет услуг по ИППП»; «Только синдромное ведение (тесты недоступны)»; «Синдромное ведение + тестирование с помощью БДТ и лечение»; «Синдромное ведение + БДТ и молекулярное тестирование, лечение + вакцинация».

narratives.en: Photograph of a health worker wearing a mask and gloves at a service window, taking a fingerprick blood sample from a client's hand passed through the window.
narratives.ar: صورة لعامل صحي يرتدي كمامة وقفازين عند نافذة تقديم الخدمة، يأخذ عينة دم بوخز الإصبع من يد عميل ممدودة عبر النافذة.
narratives.zh: 照片：一名戴口罩和手套的卫生工作者在服务窗口处，从伸过窗口的服务对象手上采集指尖血样。
narratives.es: Fotografía de un trabajador sanitario con mascarilla y guantes en una ventanilla de atención, que toma una muestra de sangre por punción digital de la mano de un usuario a través de la ventanilla.
narratives.fr: Photo d'un agent de santé portant un masque et des gants à un guichet, prélevant un échantillon de sang capillaire au bout du doigt d'un client qui tend la main à travers le guichet.
narratives.ru: Фотография: медицинский работник в маске и перчатках у окна обслуживания берет кровь из пальца у клиента, протянувшего руку через окно.

narratives.en: Photograph of a health worker in a mask showing a box of tablets to a client through a service window; the client, also masked, is seen from behind.
narratives.ar: صورة لعامل صحي يرتدي كمامة يعرض علبة أقراص على عميل عبر نافذة تقديم الخدمة؛ ويظهر العميل، الذي يرتدي كمامة أيضاً، من الخلف.
narratives.zh: 照片：一名戴口罩的卫生工作者隔着服务窗口向服务对象展示一盒片剂；同样戴着口罩的服务对象背对镜头。
narratives.es: Fotografía de un trabajador sanitario con mascarilla que muestra una caja de comprimidos a un usuario a través de una ventanilla; el usuario, también con mascarilla, se ve de espaldas.
narratives.fr: Photo d'un agent de santé masqué montrant une boîte de comprimés à un client à travers un guichet ; le client, également masqué, est vu de dos.
narratives.ru: Фотография: медицинский работник в маске показывает коробку таблеток клиенту через окно обслуживания; клиент, тоже в маске, виден со спины.

narratives.en: Green callout box reading: 'It is critical to ensure the confidentiality of clients' clinical records in both paper and electronic formats and to inform clients about such procedures.'
narratives.ar: مربع إبراز أخضر نصه: 'من الضروري ضمان سرية السجلات السريرية للعملاء بصيغتيها الورقية والإلكترونية وإبلاغ العملاء بهذه الإجراءات.'
narratives.zh: 绿色提示框，内容为：“必须确保服务对象纸质和电子形式临床记录的保密性，并告知服务对象相关程序。”
narratives.es: Recuadro verde destacado que dice: «Es fundamental garantizar la confidencialidad de los registros clínicos de los usuarios, tanto en papel como en formato electrónico, e informar a los usuarios sobre dichos procedimientos».
narratives.fr: Encadré vert indiquant : « Il est essentiel de garantir la confidentialité des dossiers cliniques des clients, sur papier comme sous forme électronique, et d'informer les clients de ces procédures. »
narratives.ru: Зеленая выноска с текстом: «Крайне важно обеспечивать конфиденциальность клинических записей клиентов как в бумажном, так и в электронном виде и информировать клиентов о таких процедурах».

narratives.en: Infographic titled 'Using QuickRes to book appointments for STI services in Namibia' showing three smartphone screens. The first is an IntraHealth Namibia social media post ('All our STI & HIV health services are FREE'), captioned 'Simple social media promotions bring clients to QuickRes'; the second is a risk assessment result page ('Time to act!'), captioned 'The Risk Assessment tool helps clients to decide what services to choose'; the third lists clinics and their services, captioned 'Clients can choose their preferred provider, date and time for their appointment'.
narratives.ar: رسم معلوماتي بعنوان 'استخدام QuickRes لحجز مواعيد خدمات العدوى المنقولة جنسياً في ناميبيا' يعرض ثلاث شاشات هواتف ذكية. الأولى منشور على وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي لمنظمة IntraHealth Namibia ('جميع خدماتنا الصحية للعدوى المنقولة جنسياً وفيروس العوز المناعي البشري مجانية')، وتعليقها 'ترويج بسيط عبر وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي يجلب العملاء إلى QuickRes'؛ والثانية صفحة نتيجة تقييم المخاطر ('حان وقت التحرك!')، وتعليقها 'تساعد أداة تقييم المخاطر العملاء على تحديد الخدمات التي يختارونها'؛ والثالثة تسرد العيادات وخدماتها، وتعليقها 'يمكن للعملاء اختيار مقدم الخدمة والتاريخ والوقت المفضل لموعدهم'.
narratives.zh: 信息图，标题为“在纳米比亚使用QuickRes预约性传播感染服务”，展示三个智能手机屏幕。第一个是IntraHealth Namibia的社交媒体帖子（“我们所有的性传播感染和艾滋病毒卫生服务均免费”），说明为“简单的社交媒体宣传将服务对象引向QuickRes”；第二个是风险评估结果页面（“该行动了！”），说明为“风险评估工具帮助服务对象决定选择哪些服务”；第三个列出诊所及其服务，说明为“服务对象可选择偏好的服务提供者以及预约日期和时间”。
narratives.es: Infografía titulada «Uso de QuickRes para reservar citas para servicios de ITS en Namibia» con tres pantallas de teléfono inteligente. La primera es una publicación en redes sociales de IntraHealth Namibia («Todos nuestros servicios de salud de ITS y VIH son GRATUITOS»), con la leyenda «Las promociones sencillas en redes sociales atraen a los usuarios a QuickRes»; la segunda es una página de resultados de evaluación del riesgo («¡Es hora de actuar!»), con la leyenda «La herramienta de evaluación del riesgo ayuda a los usuarios a decidir qué servicios elegir»; la tercera enumera centros de salud y sus servicios, con la leyenda «Los usuarios pueden elegir el proveedor, la fecha y la hora que prefieran para su cita».
narratives.fr: Infographie intitulée « Utilisation de QuickRes pour prendre rendez-vous pour des services IST en Namibie », montrant trois écrans de smartphone. Le premier est une publication d'IntraHealth Namibia sur les réseaux sociaux (« Tous nos services de santé IST et VIH sont GRATUITS »), légendée « De simples promotions sur les réseaux sociaux amènent les clients vers QuickRes » ; le deuxième est une page de résultat d'évaluation des risques (« Il est temps d'agir ! »), légendée « L'outil d'évaluation des risques aide les clients à choisir les services » ; le troisième liste des centres de santé et leurs services, légendé « Les clients peuvent choisir le prestataire, la date et l'heure de leur rendez-vous ».
narratives.ru: Инфографика под названием «Использование QuickRes для записи на прием в службы ИППП в Намибии» с тремя экранами смартфона. Первый — публикация IntraHealth Namibia в социальных сетях («Все наши услуги по ИППП и ВИЧ БЕСПЛАТНЫ») с подписью «Простая реклама в социальных сетях привлекает клиентов в QuickRes»; второй — страница результата оценки риска («Пора действовать!») с подписью «Инструмент оценки риска помогает клиентам решить, какие услуги выбрать»; третий — список клиник и их услуг с подписью «Клиенты могут выбрать удобного поставщика услуг, дату и время приема».

narratives.en: Colourful digital illustration of a person with blue skin, dark wavy hair and pink sunglasses, wearing an orange hooded sweatshirt.
narratives.ar: رسم رقمي ملون لشخص ذي بشرة زرقاء وشعر داكن مموج ونظارة شمسية وردية، يرتدي سترة برتقالية بقلنسوة.
narratives.zh: 彩色数字插画：一个蓝色皮肤、深色波浪发、戴粉色墨镜的人，身穿橙色连帽衫。
narratives.es: Ilustración digital colorida de una persona de piel azul, cabello oscuro ondulado y gafas de sol rosadas, que lleva una sudadera naranja con capucha.
narratives.fr: Illustration numérique colorée d'une personne à la peau bleue, aux cheveux sombres ondulés et aux lunettes de soleil roses, vêtue d'un sweat à capuche orange.
narratives.ru: Красочная цифровая иллюстрация: человек с синей кожей, темными волнистыми волосами и в розовых солнцезащитных очках, одетый в оранжевую толстовку с капюшоном.

narratives.en: Photograph of four people sitting together outdoors in front of a brick building, talking and smiling.
narratives.ar: صورة لأربعة أشخاص يجلسون معاً في الهواء الطلق أمام مبنى من الطوب، يتحدثون ويبتسمون.
narratives.zh: 照片：四个人在一栋砖楼前的户外坐在一起，交谈并微笑。
narratives.es: Fotografía de cuatro personas sentadas juntas al aire libre frente a un edificio de ladrillo, conversando y sonriendo.
narratives.fr: Photo de quatre personnes assises ensemble en plein air devant un bâtiment en brique, en train de discuter et de sourire.
narratives.ru: Фотография: четыре человека сидят вместе на улице перед кирпичным зданием, разговаривают и улыбаются.

narratives.en: Schematic titled 'Schematic summary of optimal STI services and case management for people who access HIV PrEP'. A coloured arc of icons leads to columns for Counselling, Prevention, Testing, Partners services, Clinical consultation, Treatment and follow-up, and Referrals and linkages, each listing key actions (e.g. provision of condoms and lubricants; rapid testing for syphilis; molecular testing for NG/CT) with a 'Jump to section' link; the leftmost column is cut off in this render. An acronym list (CT, EPT, HPV, NG) appears at bottom right.
narratives.ar: مخطط بعنوان 'ملخص تخطيطي لخدمات العدوى المنقولة جنسياً المثلى وتدبير الحالات للأشخاص الذين يحصلون على العلاج الوقائي قبل التعرض لفيروس العوز المناعي البشري'. يؤدي قوس ملون من الرموز إلى أعمدة للمشورة والوقاية والاختبار وخدمات الشركاء والاستشارة السريرية والعلاج والمتابعة والإحالات والروابط، يسرد كل منها الإجراءات الرئيسية (مثل توفير الواقيات والمزلقات؛ والاختبار السريع للزهري؛ والاختبار الجزيئي للنيسرية البنية/المتدثرة الحثرية) مع رابط 'انتقل إلى القسم'؛ والعمود الأيسر مقطوع في هذا العرض. وتظهر قائمة بالمختصرات (CT وEPT وHPV وNG) في أسفل اليمين.
narratives.zh: 示意图，标题为“为获得艾滋病毒暴露前预防者提供的最佳性传播感染服务和病例管理示意摘要”。一条彩色图标弧线引出咨询、预防、检测、性伴服务、临床问诊、治疗和随访以及转诊和衔接各栏，每栏列出关键行动（如提供安全套和润滑剂；梅毒快速检测；淋病奈瑟菌/沙眼衣原体分子检测），并附“跳转至章节”链接；此渲染图中最左侧一栏被截断。右下角有缩略语表（CT、EPT、HPV、NG）。
narratives.es: Esquema titulado «Resumen esquemático de los servicios óptimos de ITS y del manejo de casos para las personas que acceden a la PrEP contra el VIH». Un arco de iconos de colores conduce a columnas de Asesoramiento, Prevención, Pruebas, Servicios para las parejas, Consulta clínica, Tratamiento y seguimiento, y Derivación y vinculación, cada una con acciones clave (p. ej., suministro de preservativos y lubricantes; pruebas rápidas de sífilis; pruebas moleculares de NG/CT) y un enlace «Ir a la sección»; la columna del extremo izquierdo aparece cortada en esta representación. Abajo a la derecha figura una lista de siglas (CT, EPT, HPV, NG).
narratives.fr: Schéma intitulé « Résumé schématique des services IST et de la prise en charge des cas optimaux pour les personnes ayant recours à la PrEP du VIH ». Un arc d'icônes colorées mène à des colonnes Conseil, Prévention, Dépistage, Services aux partenaires, Consultation clinique, Traitement et suivi, et Orientation et liens, chacune énumérant des actions clés (p. ex. fourniture de préservatifs et de lubrifiants ; test rapide de la syphilis ; test moléculaire NG/CT) avec un lien « Aller à la section » ; la colonne la plus à gauche est tronquée dans ce rendu. Une liste d'acronymes (CT, EPT, HPV, NG) figure en bas à droite.
narratives.ru: Схема под названием «Схематическое резюме оптимальных услуг по ИППП и ведения случаев для людей, получающих ДКП ВИЧ». Цветная дуга значков ведет к столбцам «Консультирование», «Профилактика», «Тестирование», «Услуги для партнеров», «Клиническая консультация», «Лечение и последующее наблюдение» и «Направления и связь с услугами», в каждом перечислены ключевые действия (например, предоставление презервативов и лубрикантов; экспресс-тестирование на сифилис; молекулярное тестирование на NG/CT) и ссылка «Перейти к разделу»; крайний левый столбец на этом изображении обрезан. Внизу справа — список сокращений (CT, EPT, HPV, NG).

narratives.en: Photograph of a smiling health worker in a white uniform in a pharmacy store room, holding a box of tablets, with shelves of medicine boxes behind her.
narratives.ar: صورة لعاملة صحية مبتسمة ترتدي زياً أبيض في مخزن صيدلية، تحمل علبة أقراص، وخلفها رفوف عليها علب أدوية.
narratives.zh: 照片：一名身穿白色制服、面带微笑的卫生工作者在药房库房中手持一盒片剂，身后是摆满药盒的货架。
narratives.es: Fotografía de una trabajadora sanitaria sonriente con uniforme blanco en el almacén de una farmacia, que sostiene una caja de comprimidos, con estantes de cajas de medicamentos detrás.
narratives.fr: Photo d'une agente de santé souriante en uniforme blanc dans la réserve d'une pharmacie, tenant une boîte de comprimés, avec des étagères de boîtes de médicaments derrière elle.
narratives.ru: Фотография: улыбающаяся медицинская работница в белой форме на складе аптеки держит коробку таблеток; за ней полки с коробками лекарств.

narratives.en: Photograph of three young men, seen from behind, crouching and spray-painting colourful graffiti on an outdoor wall.
narratives.ar: صورة لثلاثة شبان، يظهرون من الخلف، يجثمون ويرسمون بالرذاذ رسوماً ملونة على جدار خارجي.
narratives.zh: 照片：三名年轻男子背对镜头蹲着，在户外墙上用喷漆绘制彩色涂鸦。
narratives.es: Fotografía de tres hombres jóvenes, vistos de espaldas, agachados mientras pintan con aerosol un grafiti colorido en una pared exterior.
narratives.fr: Photo de trois jeunes hommes, vus de dos, accroupis en train de peindre à la bombe un graffiti coloré sur un mur extérieur.
narratives.ru: Фотография: трое молодых людей, вид сзади, на корточках рисуют баллончиками яркое граффити на уличной стене.

narratives.en: Close-up photograph of gloved hands collecting a fingerprick blood sample into a thin capillary tube.
narratives.ar: صورة مقربة ليدين ترتديان قفازين تجمعان عينة دم بوخز الإصبع في أنبوب شعري رفيع.
narratives.zh: 特写照片：戴手套的双手将指尖血样采集到细毛细管中。
narratives.es: Fotografía en primer plano de unas manos enguantadas que recogen una muestra de sangre por punción digital en un tubo capilar fino.
narratives.fr: Gros plan de mains gantées recueillant un échantillon de sang capillaire au bout du doigt dans un fin tube capillaire.
narratives.ru: Крупный план: руки в перчатках собирают кровь из пальца в тонкую капиллярную трубку.

narratives.en: Photograph of a masked health worker in a white coat showing a tablet computer screen to a masked client seated beside him at a desk in a clinic room.
narratives.ar: صورة لعامل صحي يرتدي معطفاً أبيض وكمامة يعرض شاشة جهاز لوحي على عميل يرتدي كمامة ويجلس بجانبه إلى مكتب في غرفة بالعيادة.
narratives.zh: 照片：一名身穿白大褂、戴口罩的卫生工作者在诊室桌旁向坐在身边、同样戴口罩的服务对象展示平板电脑屏幕。
narratives.es: Fotografía de un trabajador sanitario con bata blanca y mascarilla que muestra la pantalla de una tableta a un usuario con mascarilla sentado a su lado en un escritorio de un consultorio.
narratives.fr: Photo d'un agent de santé masqué en blouse blanche montrant l'écran d'une tablette à un client masqué assis à côté de lui à un bureau dans une salle de consultation.
narratives.ru: Фотография: медицинский работник в белом халате и маске показывает экран планшета сидящему рядом за столом клиенту в маске в кабинете клиники.

narratives.en: Illustrated poster headed 'IMAGINE HELPING ALL THESE BUTTS', showing many cartoon figures seen from behind in jeans, skirts and shorts standing on a map of North America, with flags reading 'Check me out!', 'My bottom is at the top of my list!' and 'My butt is getting the attention it deserves!'. The logo 'the ANCHOR study.org' appears at the bottom.
narratives.ar: ملصق مصور يتصدره عنوان 'IMAGINE HELPING ALL THESE BUTTS'، ويعرض العديد من الشخصيات الكرتونية من الخلف ترتدي سراويل جينز وتنانير وسراويل قصيرة واقفة على خريطة أمريكا الشمالية، مع أعلام مكتوب عليها 'Check me out!' و'My bottom is at the top of my list!' و'My butt is getting the attention it deserves!'. ويظهر شعار 'the ANCHOR study.org' في الأسفل.
narratives.zh: 插画海报，标题为“IMAGINE HELPING ALL THESE BUTTS”，画面中许多身穿牛仔裤、裙子和短裤的卡通人物背对镜头站在北美洲地图上，旗帜上写着“Check me out!”、“My bottom is at the top of my list!”和“My butt is getting the attention it deserves!”。底部有“the ANCHOR study.org”标志。
narratives.es: Cartel ilustrado con el encabezado «IMAGINE HELPING ALL THESE BUTTS», que muestra muchas figuras de dibujos animados vistas de espaldas con vaqueros, faldas y pantalones cortos sobre un mapa de América del Norte, con banderas que dicen «Check me out!», «My bottom is at the top of my list!» y «My butt is getting the attention it deserves!». En la parte inferior aparece el logotipo «the ANCHOR study.org».
narratives.fr: Affiche illustrée intitulée « IMAGINE HELPING ALL THESE BUTTS », montrant de nombreux personnages dessinés vus de dos, en jean, jupe ou short, debout sur une carte de l'Amérique du Nord, avec des drapeaux portant « Check me out! », « My bottom is at the top of my list! » et « My butt is getting the attention it deserves! ». Le logo « the ANCHOR study.org » figure en bas.
narratives.ru: Иллюстрированный плакат с заголовком «IMAGINE HELPING ALL THESE BUTTS»: множество мультяшных фигур, вид сзади, в джинсах, юбках и шортах стоят на карте Северной Америки, на флажках надписи «Check me out!», «My bottom is at the top of my list!» и «My butt is getting the attention it deserves!». Внизу логотип «the ANCHOR study.org».

narratives.en: Photograph of a masked, gloved health worker in a clinic room holding an instrument beside an examination couch, where a client lies covered by a white sheet.
narratives.ar: صورة لعامل صحي يرتدي كمامة وقفازين في غرفة بالعيادة يحمل أداة بجوار سرير الفحص، حيث يستلقي عميل مغطى بملاءة بيضاء.
narratives.zh: 照片：一名戴口罩和手套的卫生工作者在诊室里手持器械站在检查床旁，床上躺着一名盖着白色床单的服务对象。
narratives.es: Fotografía de un trabajador sanitario con mascarilla y guantes en un consultorio, que sostiene un instrumento junto a una camilla de exploración donde yace un usuario cubierto con una sábana blanca.
narratives.fr: Photo d'un agent de santé masqué et ganté dans une salle de consultation, tenant un instrument à côté d'une table d'examen sur laquelle est allongé un client couvert d'un drap blanc.
narratives.ru: Фотография: медицинский работник в маске и перчатках в кабинете клиники держит инструмент возле смотровой кушетки, на которой лежит клиент, накрытый белой простыней.

narratives.en: Photograph of two young women walking and laughing together on a street beside a fenced brick wall.
narratives.ar: صورة لشابتين تسيران وتضحكان معاً في شارع بجوار جدار من الطوب يعلوه سياج.
narratives.zh: 照片：两名年轻女性在一道带栅栏的砖墙旁的街道上一起散步并大笑。
narratives.es: Fotografía de dos mujeres jóvenes que caminan y ríen juntas en una calle junto a un muro de ladrillo con verja.
narratives.fr: Photo de deux jeunes femmes qui marchent et rient ensemble dans une rue, le long d'un mur en brique surmonté d'une grille.
narratives.ru: Фотография: две молодые женщины идут и смеются на улице у кирпичной стены с оградой.
